summary: This core has very little logic specific to the board. The most distinctive part, the SLAPSTIC protection chip, is a direct re-encoding of MAME's behavioural model: it has the same mask/value table (including MAME's 0xFFFF 'UNKNOWN' placeholder, which leaves the alternate-banking path unreachable), the same states and the same order of tests. The IRQ generator lists MAME's timer schedule line by line instead of building the 32V/16V logic. The video path is a simple per-pixel scan of VRAM, char ROM and palette RAM, which is hardware-like but generic. The core has no board net names and no module for the SOS-2 video chip, and the rest is framework or memory-map material that any correct core shares with MAME.

findings.signal: Slapstic constants identical to MAME table
findings.note: Start bank 3, bank values 0x80/0x90/0xA0/0xB0, alt3 1ffc/1b5c, alt4 1fcf/0080, bitwise 1ff0/1540, 1ff3/1540..1543, 1ff8/1550 are MAME's slapstic101 mask/value pairs written out as `define equality tests, not as decoded chip logic.

findings.signal: MAME UNKNOWN sentinel copied into logic
findings.note: AT_1 is ((AD & 13'h007F)==13'hFFFF), a test that can never pass. It only makes sense as a mask/value entry copied from an emulator table whose value was marked UNKNOWN (0xffff), so the whole alt-banking path S_AT1..S_AT3 is dead logic.

findings.signal: Slapstic state machine mirrors MAME state classes
findings.note: S_DI/S_EN/S_AT1-3/S_BW1-3 map one-to-one onto idle/active/alt_valid/alt_select/alt_commit/bit_load/bit_set. The fallbacks also match: alt_valid and alt_select drop back to active on a miss, while alt_commit and bit_load have no else. A reset at $0000 is checked first in every state, as in MAME.

findings.signal: Same test priority order as MAME
findings.note: S_EN checks bank0-3, then alt, then bitwise. S_BW2 checks clear0, set0, clear1, set1, then commit. These are the exact if/else chains of the C++ test() methods. The odd/even variant of bit_set is folded into an XOR of the low address bits (bwa), which is a compact re-encoding of MAME's is_odd table swap.

findings.signal: IRQ as enumerated MAME timer schedule
findings.note: IRQ is set on lines 48/112/176/240 and cleared on 16/80/144/208. That is MAME's timer sequence (start at 48, step 32, assert when scanline&32) written out as a case list on VPOS equality, not a 32V signal latched by 16V from the raster counter.

findings.signal: Generic raster generator using MAME screen params
findings.note: A generic hcnt/vcnt generator with a counter jump to get 456x262 and 336x240 visible, matching MAME's published-spec screen parameters. The SOS-2 video chip is not modelled as a block and no H/V bit nets are named.

VRAM is addressed by {VP[7:3],HP[8:3]}, char ROM by {code,VP[2:0],HP[2:1]} with HP[0] selecting the nibble, then a palette RAM lookup, all clocked by the pixel clock. This is not MAME's tilemap/dirty-mark model. It is the obvious way to build a single tilemap in an FPGA, so it is a weak signal.

findings.signal: VRAM split into even/odd byte RAMs
findings.note: Playfield RAM is two 8-bit RAMs selected by CPU A0 and read in parallel as a 16-bit word by the video side. This is a board-style bus arrangement, unlike MAME's flat videoram array indexed tile_index*2 / *2+1.
1KB block decodes on CPUAD[15:10], slapstic CS on $6000-$7FFF, and a ROM bank that uses only BS[0], all matching MAME's map and its configure_entries(0,2)/(2,2). Any correct core would share this.

CPU clock MCLK/8, pixel clock MCLK/2, and POKEY POT inputs packed with VBLANK at bit 6 and service at bit 7 match both the board and MAME's IN0/IN1 layout. This is required for correctness, so it is neutral.
